proof:
Source: the Notation paragraph of the parent proof ("w is continuous (dominated convergence, φ continuous and bounded)"), for a general set S. This is what makes u − w integrable on B_{R+s}(0) in the parent assembly.
1. (Bound for φ.) φ is continuous with compact support, hence bounded: fix K with |φ(x)| ≤ K for all x (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support).
2. (Measurability.) Let μ_S be Lebesgue measure restricted to S and F(x, y) := u(y)φ(x − y). For each x, y ↦ F(x, y) is μ_S-a.e.-strongly measurable: u is (it is μ_S-integrable) and y ↦ φ(x − y) is continuous.
3. (Domination.) For all x and y, |F(x, y)| = |u(y)|·|φ(x − y)| ≤ K·|u(y)|.
4. (Integrable dominant.) y ↦ K·|u(y)| is μ_S-integrable, since |u| is.
5. (Continuity in the parameter.) For every y, x ↦ u(y)φ(x − y) is continuous, φ being continuous.
6. (Conclusion.) By continuity of parametric integrals under an integrable domination (continuous_of_dominated, with bound(y) = |u(y)|·K), x ↦ ∫ F(x, y) dμ_S(y) = ∫_S u(y)φ(x − y) dy is continuous. ∎
